 Fear & Greed Index falls to 14 as extreme fear grips markets
 Photo: Rostislav Uzunov / Pexels
 CNN's sentiment gauge hit its lowest level since March 30, and Bitcoin sentiment slid into the same zone
 by 
 John Chen 
 Fri 20 Nov 2026 · 11:49 EST 
 ·

 Wall Street’s mood ring just turned a very dark shade. The CNN Fear & Greed Index fell to 14 on November 20, 2026, which puts US stock sentiment firmly in “Extreme Fear” territory.
 That reading is the lowest since March 30. The slide was also fast: the index dropped 26 points over eight days, a pace that suggests investors did not ease into caution so much as sprint toward it.
 How sentiment fell apart in a week
 One week earlier, the index sat at 37. That is already fear territory, but the kind of fear that still answers emails.
 Research data puts the week-over-week decline at roughly 23 points. Over a slightly longer eight-day window, the drop stretches to 26 points.
 Over the past 30 days, the gauge has moved between 14 and 40. The current print is the bottom of that range, so this is the worst stretch of the month by the index’s own measure.
 Several of those inputs are flashing warnings right now. The ones driving the latest reading include:
 S&P 500 momentum: This component registered a score of 1. Momentum tracks whether the index is running above or below its recent trend, and a 1 means the trend has essentially lost the room.

 Stock price breadth: This measure came in at 22.8, also in extreme fear. Breadth looks at how many stocks are participating in a move, and weak breadth means the selling is not confined to a few names.
 Volatility: The VIX, often called Wall Street’s fear gauge, was reported at 13.82, with the volatility component reading extreme fear.

 Demand for junk bonds and safe-haven assets also feeds into the overall score. When investors shy away from riskier corporate debt and lean toward safer holdings, the index treats that as a sign of nerves.
 Crypto is feeling it too
 The gloom is not limited to stocks. Bitcoin ’s sentiment index stood at 12 on November 20, which also lands in the “Extreme Fear” category.
 That puts Bitcoin sentiment slightly below the equity reading of 14. The Nasdaq sat in similar territory at roughly 13.
 Bitcoin, tech stocks and the broader S&P 500 are all clustered within a couple of points of each other near the bottom of the fear scale.
 How we got here
 The March 30 reading remains the benchmark for this year’s pessimism. On that day, the index fell to approximately 10.2 amid broad weakness across markets.
 Since then, sentiment has bounced between fear and extreme fear rather than settling into anything resembling calm. The current reading of 14 does not match the March trough, but it is the closest the index has come since then.
 The gap between the two lows is worth noting. At roughly 10.2 versus 14, the market is a few points away from revisiting its spring panic, not miles from it.
 What this means for investors
 Extreme fear readings tend to change behavior. Research findings suggest the current environment may lead to pulled-back investment activity, with trading volumes potentially staying subdued as investors wait for clearer signals.
 The research points to investors possibly favoring value stocks or assets seen as safe havens while stepping away from speculative bets.
 For crypto, the outlook described in the research is a risk-off attitude paired with heightened volatility.
 The more useful signal may be in the components. An S&P 500 momentum reading of 1 and breadth at 22.8 describe a market where weakness is broad and the trend has turned decisively negative.
 For Bitcoin holders, the key question is whether crypto sentiment keeps tracking equities or starts to decouple. With Bitcoin’s index at 12 and the Nasdaq near 13, the two are currently moving like dance partners.
 Watch the March 30 low as well. A drop below approximately 10.2 would mark a new low for the year, while a move back toward the 30-day high of 40 would indicate the panic was more of a flinch than a collapse.
